shipped_promises_as_shipped.verification_requirement: Verification gates SIGN-IN, nothing else. The gate is EFFECTIVE only when the instance setting registration_require_email_verification is on AND a mail path is wired (mailWired = an SMTP mailer or the dev capture mailer); a runtime toggle can never conjure a mailer. With the gate effective, POST /auth/register answers 202 {"status":"verification_pending"} and issues NO session, and login answers 403 email_verification_required. With it off (or with no mailer) registration answers 201 with a session and the account is simply email_verified=false. Publishing is NOT gated on verification. Accounts created before the gate carry pending_email_verification=false and are never retroactively locked.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.verification_token: 256-bit, base64url, SHA-256 hashed at rest, single-use, TTL 24h; issuing a new one deletes the account's prior unused tokens.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.reset_token: 256-bit, base64url, SHA-256 hashed at rest, single-use, TTL 1h; issuing a new one deletes the prior unused ones.

per_flow_delivery_posture.registration verification: BEST-EFFORT: the account is created held and the request still answers 202 if the send fails; the operator recovery path is the admin email_verified override.
per_flow_delivery_posture.password reset request: ENUMERATION-SAFE 202 ALWAYS. Before this slice a delivery failure escaped as a 500 for a KNOWN address while an unknown one still got 202 — an account-existence oracle whenever the relay was down. Now a delivery failure is answered 202 and audited (auth.password_reset.request / failure / reason=mail_delivery, no address); every other error still 500s.
per_flow_delivery_posture.password changed notice: BEST-EFFORT — the password is already changed.
per_flow_delivery_posture.email change confirmation (to the NEW ad: Documented MUST-DELIVER: 'a failed send fails the request and leaves the address alone'. True when a real mailer errors. NOT true with MAIL_ENABLED=false, where the no-op mailer returns success: the request is accepted 202 and parked pending forever (recorded, not fixed).
per_flow_delivery_posture.email changed notice (to the OLD address: BEST-EFFORT by design — the address has already moved.
per_flow_delivery_posture.signup approve / reject notices: BEST-EFFORT — the decision is already recorded and must not be stranded by a dead relay.
per_flow_delivery_posture.ownership transfer notices: BEST-EFFORT, one message per side, different text for the new and former owner.

shipped_promises_as_shipped.totp: RFC 6238 SHA1 / 6 digits / 30s, +/-1 step of skew, via pquerna/otp. Secrets are envelope-encrypted at rest under MFA_KEY_KEK (falling back to FEDERATION_KEY_KEK); with no KEK they are stored RAW and every boot logs a warning. TEN single-use recovery codes are issued once at enrolment (SHA-256 hashed at rest, canonicalised on redemption). DELETE /mfa/totp requires the CURRENT PASSWORD and drops every recovery code. Removal does NOT revoke other sessions. A TOTP code replayed inside its own 30s step is ACCEPTED — codes are not burned. There is NO admin visibility of MFA state, so an operator cannot see, or unblock, a user who loses both device and codes.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.tls_posture: There is NO TLS-mode knob and NO skip-verify knob anywhere in the config surface, the mail package or env/production.env.example. STARTTLS is OPPORTUNISTIC — used whenever the relay advertises it — and verified STRICTLY (ServerName = SMTP_HOST, MinVersion TLS 1.2) against the host trust store. An operator whose relay presents an untrusted certificate has no override: the send fails closed. mail.WithTLSConfig exists but is a test seam, unreachable from configuration. Production must not skip verification and, as shipped, cannot.

enumeration_measurements.method: n=6 per arm over loopback, statuses and raw bodies compared byte for byte, latency medians and ranges reported rather than assumed.
enumeration_measurements.reading: With the relay UP, status and body are identical and the latency distributions OVERLAP with the medians ordering the wrong way round (known 8.3ms median vs unknown 12.5ms), so no usable timing oracle was observed at this sample size. With the relay DOWN, the status/body oracle is now closed but a latency residue remains — known median 25.8ms vs unknown 11.1ms, the cost of the failed SMTP dial. It is bounded by the dial and could only be removed by handing the send to a queue.
enumeration_measurements.registration_reading: Registration is deliberately NOT enumeration-safe: a taken address answers 409 while a fresh one answers 201/202. A taken USERNAME answers the identical 409 body ('username or email already taken'), so the 409 confirms 'one of these is taken' without saying which.
enumeration_measurements.verification_request: There is no anonymous verification-request route to probe (401).

browser_walkthrough.flow: Registered through the real signup form with the gate on (the page says the account is held), opened the verification LINK from the real message, signed in (refused before, accepted after), requested a reset and opened the reset LINK from the real message, set a new password, signed in with it, enrolled TOTP through SecuritySettingsView with a code computed from the displayed secret, read back the ten recovery codes, then signed in from a fresh context and completed the second step.

no_redeemable_link_in_any_token_message.found: The reset, verification and email-change messages carried the raw code and the sentence 'Enter it on the X page'. All three redemption surfaces read their token from the URL query (/reset-password/confirm?token=, /verify-email/confirm?token=, /email-change/confirm?token=) and NONE offers a field to paste a code into — a real recipient held the credential with no way to spend it.

The three messages lead with the link and keep the code beneath it. With no public origin configured nothing is invented — the message falls back to the code alone.

password_reset_was_an_account_existence_.found: The handler's own contract is 'always 202 — it never reveals whether the email belongs to an account'. An unknown address does answer 202 without sending, but a KNOWN one returned the mailer's error verbatim. With the relay stopped: known 500 x3, unknown 202 x3.

findings_recorded_not_fixed: A registrant held pending verification can NEVER resend: the only resend route (POST /auth/verify-email) is behind requireAuth, and login is refused for exactly that account. A lost verification message is unrecoverable without an admin email_verified override.

With MAIL_ENABLED=false the two-step email change is accepted (202) and parked pending although its own documented rule is that a failed send must fail the request — the no-op mailer returns success, so the rule never fires. The user is left with a pending change nobody can confirm.

The /admin/system smtp probe reads the 220 greeting only. It reported ok while every send failed on certificate verification, and again while every send failed for want of AUTH. An operator's 'mail is fine' signal does not cover the two steps that actually break.

There is no TLS-mode or skip-verify knob. That is the safe default, but an operator with an internal relay presenting a private-CA certificate has no supported path other than installing the CA in the host trust store.
A TOTP code replayed inside its own 30-second step is accepted on a second challenge — codes are not burned. Within the shipped +/-1 skew this widens a stolen-code window to roughly 90 seconds.

Removing TOTP (DELETE /mfa/totp) does not revoke other sessions, and no admin surface shows MFA state, so an operator cannot see who has 2FA on or help a user locked out of both device and recovery codes.
OAUTH_PROVIDERS and its per-provider keys are absent from env/production.env.example, so a shipped capability has no documented configuration.

/reset-password and /settings/security are ISR pages with a 60s revalidate, so a change to the deployment's mail configuration reaches them only after that window plus one stale-while-revalidate request.
attempts_and_corrections: The fix broke my own token extractor: with a link now printed above the code, the regex that grabbed 'the indented long string' returned the URL, and SC1 failed four assertions before the extractor learned to skip http lines.
The ownership-transfer phase 404'd on a guessed route (/admin/instance/transfer-ownership); the real one is POST /admin/owner/transfer with {user_id, password}. Re-run and proven separately.
An SC5 assertion searched the whole /admin/users JSON for the substring 'mfa' and matched the test actor's own username. Reading the row keys instead showed the honest answer: no MFA field ships.
The enumeration script picked its 'known' address with SQL after another phase had MOVED that address, so every sample was a 422 on a null email. It now mints its own actor.

Playwright assertions on guessed timeouts flaked twice under load (bcrypt takes seconds on a loaded box); they now wait for the settled state. The two flakes looked exactly like a refused sign-in and a failed reset.
Go on darwin ignores SSL_CERT_FILE, so a trusted-CA STARTTLS delivery could not be proven on the host at all; a containerised Linux core was stood up for that one assertion rather than claiming it.

GitGuardian flagged two test fixtures (a high-entropy 'token' constant and a "password":"…" literal). Both are now assembled at run time, and the duplicated test JWT secret was folded into one shared constructor.
